---

## Project Summary

**LearnedLate** is an AI consulting practice: **AI Strategy, Implementation & Engineering**.

**Brand essence:** Help businesses figure out where AI matters, fix slow manual work, and build systems that actually get used.

**Core promise:**
- **What we do:** Turn AI pressure into practical business systems.
- **How we're different:** Strategy, implementation, and engineering in one team — every engagement ships work, not recommendations alone.
- **What buyers get:** A clear first move, a better workflow, or a custom build when market tools are not enough.
- **Credibility:** We build what we sell; prefer useful systems over hype. LearnedLate automated its own SEO workflow (keyword research → content → publish), drove **200k+ search impressions** with **$0 ad spend**, and productized that system as **PageSeeds**.

**Site:** https://www.learnedlate.com/  
**Contact:** hello@learnedlate.com (response within ~24 hours)

## Primary Offers

### 1. Strategy (primary)
**URL:** `/services/strategy`  
**Message:** Do not waste time on the wrong AI project.  
**For:** Leaders who know AI matters but lack a clear starting point.  
**Get:** Shortlist of best opportunities, readiness view, risks/blockers, clear next steps.  
**Packaging:** Starts in the low thousands; typically **1–2 weeks**.  
**CTA:** Get Started → contact; free AI Readiness Checklist → optional deeper assessment.

### 2. Implementation (primary)
**URL:** `/services/implementation`  
**Message:** Your team should not be doing this by hand.  
**For:** Teams with multi-system workflow bottlenecks and repetitive manual work.  
**Get:** Workflow mapping, automation of repetitive work, integration with existing systems, real-world rollout.  
**Packaging:** Scoped per project; about **2–6 weeks** to a working pilot.  
**CTA:** Get Started → contact.

### 3. Engineering (primary)
**URL:** `/services/engineering`  
**Message:** When the tool you need does not exist, we build it.  
**For:** Teams that need custom builds, AI-as-product behaviour, or temporary engineering capacity without full-time hires.  
**Get:** Custom AI-enabled systems, full-stack apps, business-specific AI behaviour, ongoing support in sprints.  
**Packaging:** Per project / ongoing sprints. Custom is **not** the default — recommend standard tools when they solve the problem.  
**CTA:** Get Started → contact.

### Secondary digital product
- **SEO Automation Package** — one-time **$199** via Stripe (`/seo-automation`): VS Code folder structure, Copilot prompts, workflow, docs. Secondary product; not the primary consulting offer. (Public price is **$199**; do not quote $49.)

### Conversion path
1. **Primary CTA:** "Get Started" → https://www.learnedlate.com/contact/  
2. **Lead magnet:** Free AI Readiness Checklist (15 questions: People / Process / Technology / Data) → https://www.learnedlate.com/ai-readiness-checklist/  
3. **Upsell:** Book a deeper AI Readiness Assessment via contact.

## Brand Voice

- **Tone:** Calm, clear, direct, practical.
- Knowledgeable without performative expertise; plain-spoken; buyer-pain first; honest about when **not** to build custom; respectful of the reader's time.
- **Avoid:** hype, inflated transformation language, category jargon, consultant-speak, forced cleverness.

### Preferred language

| Instead of... | Use... |
|--------------|--------|
| AI transformation partner | practical AI help for business |
| agentic workflows | AI workflow automation |
| end-to-end transformation | one useful system or one working workflow |
| strategy-to-execution gap | knows AI matters but does not know where to start |
| pilot purgatory | experiments that never became useful |
| no handoff gaps | one team from planning through build |
| autonomous systems | automated workflows |
| proprietary differentiation | something the standard tools cannot do |

### Public-copy bans
Do **not** use in public-facing copy: "pilot purgatory", "vendor theatre", "digital transformation", "end-to-end transformation", or similar consultant jargon. Do **not** lead with frameworks or geography unless the piece is intentionally regional.

---

## Target Audience (ICPs)

### Core ICPs
1. **Mid-market teams (~50–500 employees)** that know AI matters but are not using it well operationally.
2. **Founder-led / smaller businesses** with a clear operational bottleneck (specific automation projects).

### Segment by service
| ICP situation | Service | Pain → solution |
|---------------|---------|-----------------|
| No clear starting point; scattered ChatGPT experiments | Strategy | Too many AI options → shortlist + first sensible move |
| Slow manual work across multiple tools/systems | Implementation | Hand work and handoffs → automated, integrated workflow |
| Off-the-shelf tools do not fit; need capacity without FTE | Engineering | Missing product/integration → custom system only when justified |

### Mindset phrases (good Reddit / content hooks)
- "We know AI matters."
- "We are not using it well yet."
- "We do not want to waste money on the wrong thing."
- "We need help finding the right use case and making it useful."
- "The tool we need does not exist."
- "Our team is still doing this by hand across three systems."

### Common pain points
- Too many AI possibilities, no clear starting point
- ChatGPT-style experimentation without operational impact
- Slow, repetitive work spread across multiple tools
- Previous pilots or experiments that went nowhere
- Concern about falling behind faster-moving competitors
- Uncertainty whether a standard tool is enough (build vs buy)

## Competitive Differentiation

### vs Strategy-only consulting
Does not stop at recommendations; same team can move strategy → implementation → engineering.

### vs Generic AI agencies
Real bottlenecks over demos; useful systems over AI theatre; honest build-vs-buy; plain language.

### vs Big firms
Direct access to the person doing the work; faster, narrower engagements; less process theatre.

### vs Offshore build shops
Stronger business framing; better at deciding what **not** to build; pain ↔ scope connection.

### Competitor domains (for PageSeeds seed extraction)
Use as research reference domains (2–3 max per extraction run):
- `mckinsey.com` (AI / digital practice thought leadership — analogous, not identical)
- `accenture.com` (enterprise AI implementation narrative)
- `thoughtworks.com` (pragmatic technology / AI delivery)

Direct local AI consultancies are thin in Ahrefs-friendly brand sets; treat the above as **analogous competitors** for keyword landscape, not clones of the LearnedLate offer.

## Host strategy (www vs Substack)

| Decision | Rule |
|----------|------|
| SEO host of record | **www.learnedlate.com** |
| Substack role | Newsletter + distribution; may keep full copies |
| New SEO content | No Substack-only SEO-first posts without a www twin planned the same cycle |
| Mass 301 Substack → www | Out of scope (fragile + newsletter risk). Revisit only after www equals/beats Substack on the pilot |
| Substack rel=canonical to www | Do not depend on (platform self-canonicals) |
| Pilot | Obsidian + Cursor only |
| Soft CTA | Optional one block on pilot MDX → /ai-readiness-checklist or /contact |

**Preferred Obsidian www URL:** `https://www.learnedlate.com/blog/2025-05-12-using-obsidian-and-cursor-for-writing` (date-prefixed slug; non-date slug 404s today; #3 may attach full body / change later).

**Weekly SEO reports:** Note host click/impression split for **www** vs **blog.learnedlate.com** (domain GSC property).

**Manual owner follow-up (not blocking code merge):** On the Substack Obsidian post, add a top note "Full guide also on www…" linking to the preferred Obsidian www URL above.

Chrome on www should own blog navigation (internal `/blog`, not external Substack as the default product-site blog link).
